aboutParagraphs: Hornets Nest is Charlotte's most famous public course — the front nine plays open parkland while the back nine dives into the wooded Piedmont, a split personality that makes the round feel like two courses in one. It's the anchor of Charlotte's disc golf scene and a regular stop on the national tournament circuit.

Free to play with concrete tees and DISCatcher baskets, the course offers multiple pin positions and a tournament island hole that only comes into play for events. From the standard red pins it plays 6,184 feet at par 58.
The back nine's woods are where Hornets Nest earns its reputation — tight lines, water in play, and a finish that demands your full attention.

signatureHoleDescription: Hole 17 is Hornets Nest's signature: 577 feet of par 4 through the heart of the wooded back nine. From the tee you're threading a gap in the Piedmont timber; from the landing zone you're choosing a line at a basket the woods guard from every angle. It's the hole that turns a good round into a great one — and the one that makes first-timers respect Charlotte's home course.
localTips: The front nine is open and forgiving; the back nine is where the course earns its reputation. Water comes into play on the back side, and the tournament island hole only appears for events. Free to play — go early on weekends to beat the crowds.
